timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So what exactly is an Azure landing zone? Is it like a VM?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: No. It's a pre-configured environment with governance baked in from the start.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How is that different from just creating a subscription?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: A subscription is just a billing boundary. A landing zone has policies, networking, and security.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: You mentioned two types. Platform and application?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Platform handles core infrastructure. Connectivity, identity, management. Application hosts your workloads.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: And enterprise-scale? Is that the big-company version?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It uses management group hierarchies and dedicated subscriptions for scale.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What are the six design areas you mentioned?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Identity, topology, management, security, governance, and deployment automation.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So everything is planned out before you even deploy a workload?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Build the foundation right, and everything on top is solid.
